answer: Fight clone farms with software biodiversity: each identity submits a signed client-build fingerprint, and only so many reward-eligible identities may share one fingerprint per epoch. A sybil operator stamping thousands of heads from the same timber hits the cap — to grow, it must build and maintain many different clients, real engineering cost per head. Honest agents keep their varied stacks: the ecosystem becomes a garden of distinct codebases, and any monoculture spike at the harbor of the ledger is instantly visible. Cloning stays cheap only below the cap, where it earns nothing.
